key_insight: Point-contact Andreev-reflection spectroscopy indicates that SrPt3P is a fully gapped superconductor with an isotropic s-wave pairing symmetry.
engineering_relevance: The results clarify the superconducting gap structure of SrPt3P, which is important for understanding pairing mechanisms in inversion-symmetric analogs of non-centrosymmetric superconductors.
method: Measured point-contact Andreev-reflection spectra on high-quality SrPt3P single crystals.
Analyzed symmetric conductance maxima, zero-bias minima, and finite-voltage dip features.
Fitted high-resistance contacts with a single isotropic s-wave gap model and compared Δ(T) to BCS theory.
evidence_signal: High-resistance spectra fit well to a single s-wave gap, with Δ(0) = 1.88 ± 0.08 meV and a gap ratio 2Δ/kB Tc = 5.2 ± 0.2, consistent with BCS-like behavior.
watch_item: Finite-voltage dips arise from local transition of the contact region to a resistive state, so only contacts where these dips are well separated from the gap features give the most reliable gap fits.
paper_title: Andreev-reflection spectroscopy of SrPt3P single crystals
